about.title: Crescent City Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Crescent City may be small, but its traffic corridors — Route 101, US-101, 5th Street, and L Street — see a steady flow of collisions each year, with local records showing 21 injury crashes and 32 people hurt in the most recent reporting year. Tuesday midday hours tend to bring more reported crashes, likely tied to local commuting and errand patterns. Whether your collision happened near the harbor, along the highway corridor, or on a residential street, the aftermath is the same: medical bills, missed work, and an insurance adjuster who may call before you've even seen a doctor. We don't practice law — we evaluate the crash, deal with insurers, and help protect your right to recover. There's no cost for a free case review, and no obligation to move forward.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before You Talk to the Insurer

items.title: California's Fault Rules Can Affect Your Recovery
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you're partly responsible for the crash, you may still recover damages reduced by your share of fault. We can help make sure your percentage of blame isn't overstated by the other side.

items.title: The Clock Starts Running Fast
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the crash date to file a lawsuit, but claims against a government entity — like a road defect on a city or county street — can require notice in as little as six months. Missing that shorter window can end your claim before it starts.

items.title: What You Say to the Insurer Matters
items.desc: There's no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering under California law, but a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer can be used to minimize what you're owed. We can handle that communication and help preserve evidence from the scene before it disappears.

items.question: How much does it cost to get a free case review?
items.answer: Nothing. We offer free case reviews, and our team typically works on contingency, meaning we only get paid if you recover money. You never pay out of pocket to speak with us or to have your case reviewed.

items.question: I was in a crash on 5th Street in Crescent City — should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney, since insurers often use those statements to reduce what they owe. We can communicate with the insurance company on your behalf and help protect your claim from the start.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in California?
items.answer: In most cases you have two years from the date of the crash to file a lawsuit, but if a government entity is involved — such as a poorly maintained road — the notice deadline can be as short as six months. Because these deadlines vary and evidence can disappear quickly, it's worth talking to an attorney as soon as possible.
